Welcome to Update's 4th mini-conference!

When: November 21–22 2026, 10:00–18:00
Where: Datorföreningen Update, Svartbäcksgatan 65, 753 33 #Uppsala

The conference and hackathon are free for anyone to attend. You're encouraged to bring along friends and peculiar computer hardware!

Please sign up if you plan to attend!
Sign-up: https://dud-poll.inf.tu-dresden.de/CoQa14jXHQ/

We hope to see you there!

=== Schedule ===

==== Saturday, November 21 2026 ====

10:00 – Arrival
10:15 – This Internet thing. Kaj Kjellgren (DE-CIX)
11:00 – From PDP-1 to Playstation 2 – A brief history of #computergraphics. Angelo Papenhoff (Obsolescence Guaranteed)
11:45 – The #programming language POP-11. Herbert Lange (University of Gothenburg)
12:30 – Lunch break
13:30 – Decompiling ancient #software. John Källén
14:15 – Floppy #preservation: A beginner's first steps. Pontus Pihlgren (Datorföreningen Update)
15:00 – Coffee break
15:15 – A #Datapoint 2200 resurrects – From IKEA kit to running. Mattis Lind (Dalby Datormuseum)
16:00 – The missing #LINC in #retrocomputing. Lars Brinkhoff (ICtech)
16:45 – Guided tour of Update's premises
18:00 – Collective pizza order and mingle

Abstracts and more info:
https://wiki.dfupdate.se/projekt:mini-conference

==== Sunday, November 22 2026 ====

all day starting 10:00 – #PDP-12 #hackathon

The PDP-12 is a laboratory computer introduced by #Digital Equipment Corporation (#DEC) in 1969. Only few dozen remain in existence today. Datorföreningen Update owns a PDP-12 called "Elsa", but it stopped working. You can read more about it in Update's newsletter Uptime 8 2023 (in Swedish).
https://wiki.dfupdate.se/_media/uptime:uptime-8-2023.pdf

In this hackathon, we will try to bring Elsa back to working condition. We will flip switches, read schematic diagrams, swap circuit boards, and observe signals. If this sounds intimidating, don't worry, we will learn from each other as we go. Everybody is welcome to participate, regardless of previous knowledge. Join us in this quest to bring Elsa back to live!

Drop in whenever you like. Food plans will be made spontaneously.

#computerhistory
